text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated GPU mem reclamation and paging observed on runtime-pool-3. 98% of requests experiencing latency spikes. Trigger: mem-pressure > 90% for 3x samplings.

oncall-maya: on it — I'm taking pager. starting live triage. @support-ops can you flag any customer-facing errors?

support-ops: seeing ~120 5xx gateway errors over last 10m from region eu-west-1, mostly from customers on dedicated capacity. No public incident page yet.

toncall-maya: quick mitigation idea — reduce max_batch_size on pool 3 to 1 for low-latency routes, and drain long-running KV caches. I'll coord with infra.

tj: +1. Put canary change on a single node first, then roll if stable. Also want GPU mem dumps from the slowest pods.

sam-sre: pulling logs now. running: kubectl -n prod logs deploy/runtime-pool-3 --since=15m | grep -i "OOM\|evict\|kvcache" -A3 -B1

sam-sre: log snippet:
```
[13:42:10] runtime: alloc 1.9G -> total 12.1G (100%)
[13:42:11] kvcache: insert failed, evicting oldest segment
[13:42:11] gpu: mem reclaim 85% -> paging start
[13:42:12] runtime: OOM-avoid triggered, refusing new requests
```

kevin: hypothesis: large prefix-heavy requests + continuous batching are growing KV and not getting evicted fast enough; we may be hitting fragmentation rather than pure allocation.

maria: can we toggle aggressive kvcache eviction policy (ttl=20s, max_entries=20k) as a live experiment? That should free pages fast but could increase customer token cost.

oncall-maya: action items: 1) tj will rollout batch_size=1 canary to node-7; 2) sam-sre will attach GPU pmap and collect fragmentation metrics; 3) kevin will push temporary KV eviction tune; 4) maria will inform PM/sales about potential customer retries. I'll update status every 5m.

tj: starting canary now on node-7: deploy patch command: kubectl -n prod set env deploy/runtime-pool-3 BATCH_MAX=1 --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-7

tj: canary deployed. watching 1/1. request latency on that node down from 1.2s -> 320ms within 90s.

sam-sre: attached pmap and nvml snapshot. small extract:
```
GPU0: total 40G, used 38.6G, free 1.4G
large free blocks: 1x1.2G, 6x64M, fragmentation_ratio=0.28
active allocations: 7200 (avg size 5.3MB)
```

kevin: fragmentation_ratio 0.28 suggests compaction might help. live compaction not in prod, but reassigning requests to fresh process frees contiguous space. Plan: drain and restart problematic pods one at a time.

maria: contacting affected account owners: sending short note that we're investigating memory pressure and may see transient 5xxs.

oncall-maya: customer impact: medium — dedicated customers see retries; hosted API small percent degraded. No P0.

tj: executing rolling restart on pool-3 with concurrency 1 to avoid cascading pressure. command: kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/runtime-pool-3 --timeout=10m && sleep 30s between pods

sam-sre: capturing timeline entries to paste into the RCA doc:
- 13:40 alert triggered by mem-pressure metric
- 13:42 first OOM-avoid log and kvcache insert failures
- 13:44 batch_size canary -> latency improves on node-7
- 13:47 nvml snapshot shows fragmentation ratio 0.28
- 13:50 rolling restart initiated

kevin: hypothesis thread: primary cause = KV cache growth + large batched prefixes causing allocation churn -> fragmentation -> paging. Secondary contributor = long-lived allocations in certain model variants.

oncall-maya: temporary mitigations applied: decreased batching, aggressive kvcache eviction on pool-3, rolling pod restarts. Monitoring for recurrence for 30m.

maria: will follow up with customers in 1h with update.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: incident-id INC-388000-alloc-surge. Current status: mitigated (degraded -> stable). Next: create postmortem, include timeline, hypotheses, and proposed long-term fixes (kvcache TTL defaults, compaction work, model mem safety limits). :white_check_mark:

oncall-maya: thanks everyone — tagging for postmortem owners: @kevin (lead hypothesis), @sam-sre (telemetry), @tj (mitigations). I'll hand back on-call in 10m. :thumbsup:
